newsitem.title: USA: Police search for suspect in Calif. bomb plot.
newsitem.headline: Police search for suspect in Calif. bomb plot.

text.p: Police in northern California searched on Monday for a man suspected of masterminding a series of bombings to disrupt his trial on drug charges.

Authorities say Vallejo resident Kevin Robinson, 29, is wanted on suspicion of conspiracy and explosives violations after bombs damaged a court and a bank in Vallejo, 35 miles (50 kms) northeast of San Francisco, in the last 10 days. A third bomb was disarmed.

News reports said police believed Robinson hired two other men who are already in custody to carry out the bombings to prevent his trial on drugs charges that was due to start in a nearby town on Monday. If convicted on those charges, Robinson could face a life prison sentence, the reports said.

"It's our opinion that he has conspired with these other individuals in an effort to do whatever he possibly can do to stop his trial from starting today," Vallejo police chief Robert Nichelini told reporters.

Vallejo police spokesman Lt. Ron Jackson said police believed it was a "bombing for hire." He said police considered Robinson "armed and dangerous" and were concentrating their search for him in the Vallejo area, although he might try to leave the area.

San Francisco's KCBS radio reported that an acquaintance of Robinson had contacted authorities about his possible surrender. It said Robinson could turn himself in on Monday. The station also reported that police may be looking for a fourth suspect in the case.
Authorities say the Vallejo bombings are not connected to three mail bombs found in the San Diego area in recent days.

Police said on Sunday they had seized 500 pounds (230 kg) of dynamite and arrested two men suspected of carrying out the bombings to subvert the justice system. They found the huge haul of dynamite in a garage while searching a house in Vallejo on Sunday evening.
"We located approximately 500 pounds of dynamite in individual sticks. That translates to about five or six cases of dynamite," Jackson said.

Police ordered residents to evacuate nearby houses as a safety precaution while they removed the dynamite. They said they arrested one suspect, Francis Ernestberg, 40, at a house in Vallejo early on Sunday. He was booked into Solano County jail for investigation of conspiracy, explosives violations and burglary.
Police also found a car with 61 sticks of dynamite in the trunk. The suspects were apparently planning to use the car bomb in an attack that could have been catastrophic, investigators said.
Later on Sunday, police arrested a second suspect, Oston Osotonu, 24, who was jailed on a no-bail warrant charging him with conspiracy and explosives violations, police said.
Police said the dynamite they recovered had been stolen. They believed they had found most of the missing dynamite.
Two bombs exploded in Vallejo in the last week, one outside a courthouse and one outside a bank. Both pre-dawn bombings caused damage but no injuries.
Last weekend, police also found and disarmed a bomb containing at least 30 sticks of dynamite that had been placed outside a public library that houses a police evidence room.
Police say the bank bombing may have been a diversion to disguise the bombers' motive.
